source_refs.note: Uncertainty in Digital Instruments: a main subheading of 1.3 Uncertainty in measurement, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 8-9.

blocks.text: Some modern measuring instruments have a digital scale. We usually estimate one digit beyond what is certain: with a digital scale, this is reflected in some fluctuations of the last digit. If the last digit fluctuates by 1 or 2, write down that last digit. If fluctuation is more than 2 or so in the last digit, it may mean that the reading is being influenced by some factor such as air currents. Regardless of the reason, a large fluctuation may mean that the displayed digit is not really significant.

The indication of uncertainty in a recorded value has been simplified using significant figures. If a measurement is recorded using the knowledge of significant figures, then its last digit, which is an estimation, is an indication of the accuracy of the recorded value.
